question: to the Commission Catarina Martins (The Left) Subject:

In recent weeks, several storms have hit Portugal, causing a wave of destruction on an unprecedented scale. In addition to causing damage to homes, vehicles, trees, businesses, electricity and communications networks, as well as to the water supply, the gales and floods have devastated the agricultural sector in the regions concerned. For most farmers, in addition to the damage suffered, this means starting again almost from scratch. Beyond this direct impact on farmers, there will be consequences for consumers as a result of reduced or limited agricultural production, whether due to rising food prices or supply shortages. In light of the above: 1.
Will the European Commission take all necessary measures to compensate farmers for the damages they have suffered, and also to support the recovery of their businesses?
What measures does the European Commission intend to take to ensure, in accordance with Article 39 TFEU, the availability of supplies and to ensure that supplies reach consumers at reasonable prices?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.7.2026) Under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), in its 2023-2027 CAP Strategic Plan (CSP), Portugal has programmed support for the restoration of agricultural and forestry potential following natural disasters, adverse climatic events or catastrophic events amounting to EUR 23.6 million of the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) available for farmers and forest owners. In addition, following the recent omnibus simplification1, Member States can mobilise CSP funding for crisis payments that compensate for production losses due to such events. The Portuguese authorities can use this option. To provide support to Portugal, the Commission proposed to allocate EUR 30 million from the agricultural crisis reserve, which was endorsed by the Member States. Portugal shall compensate the most affected farmers for their economic losses. Furthermore, Portugal may grant additional national support up to maximum of 200% of the EU emergency financial contribution. The Commission will now adopt its proposal, and it will enter into force the day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. This will allow farmers to receive support as soon as possible. Regarding the impact on the availability of supply and prices to consumers, the EU internal market for agricultural products ensures the free movement of agri-food goods across borders. The CAP integrates the agricultural sector into the broader single market to ensure fair competition, food security, a level playing field for farmers and reasonable prices for consumers.
